latest_release.body:
# pdfcpu v0.16.4

This is a security update for crafted PDFs and form or create data that could cause excessive CPU or memory use or terminate a
process. 

Additive Go API  Changes: `types.DecodeStreamFunc` and `types.NewLazyObjectStreamObjectWithDecoder`. 
Existing constructors and signatures remain unchanged.
Requires Go 1.26 or later.

**Release binaries were built with [Go 1.27.3](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#go1.27.3), which includes security fixes for `crypto/x509`.**

**1) Unbounded object traversal — [GHSA-2623-w998-vcr4](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/security/advisories/GHSA-2623-w998-vcr4):**

Long chains of PDF objects could exhaust the Go stack and terminate the process during optimization while reading,
annotation removal, or page migration. These paths now use iterative traversal. The fix preserves long valid chains,
handles objects whose value is another reference, and bounds error-path output.

Fix: [0bb00190](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/commit/0bb001901ef160aa75e882d839ee2997d56fdcb2).

**2) Repeated stream data — [GHSA-pr6x-vqwr-4hj2](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/security/advisories/GHSA-pr6x-vqwr-4hj2):**

Shared or nested stream aliases and oversized declared lengths could make a small PDF retain unbounded encoded or
decoded data. Encoded streams now count toward the existing per-read budget, lengths past the end of the input no
longer size buffers, and compressed xref entries that share one current object-stream index are rejected.

Filtered decodes through `XRefTable.DecodeStream` and lazy object streams each receive a separate cumulative allowance
`A = max(1 GiB, 2 × MaxDecodeBytes)`; both default to 1 GiB. The allowances count cumulative decoding, not live memory.
Object streams remain lazy, image extraction remains subject to its per-stream and image limits, and a negative
`MaxDecodeBytes` disables these limits.

Fix: [82c88cec](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/commit/82c88cecdee7dac398bebf06d0bdd28728235a57).

**3) Poster tile grids — [GHSA-g5q6-53hx-f68j](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/security/advisories/GHSA-g5q6-53hx-f68j):**

A crafted page size could make `poster` create an unbounded number of tile definitions and output pages, consuming
excessive CPU and memory. Poster output is now limited to 1,000 tiles per source page, and oversized grids are rejected
before page content is transformed or tile objects are allocated. Zero, negative and non-finite page or tile dimensions
are rejected.

Tiles produced by `poster`, `cut` and `ndown` now share one resource dictionary per source page instead of carrying a
copy each. With a margin, each tile references the shared page content through a content array instead of embedding a
copy of it. Rendered output is unchanged.

Fix: [a9725db6](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/commit/a9725db622f32c519fee90c1733b779ccd5dd598).

**4) Create table dimensions — [GHSA-cphg-88q6-whwh](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/security/advisories/GHSA-cphg-88q6-whwh):**

Table `rows` and `cols` in a `create` template were unbounded, so a few hundred bytes of JSON could make create
allocate and render without limit. All tables of a template now share a limit of 100,000 rows plus columns. A table
whose `anchor` is invalid, or given together with `pos`, is now rejected; previously its remaining validation was
skipped.

Fix: [5367e878](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/commit/5367e878f7766b94dd5f7e9e3128e1ab5f9b30b6).

**5) Unbounded page numbers — [GHSA-gx4m-7r76-vpww](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/security/advisories/GHSA-gx4m-7r76-vpww):**

A large page number in a `create` template or form-fill data could make pdfcpu allocate excessive memory or stall.
`create` now limits additions to 1,000 pages beyond the existing document; `form fill` and `form multifill` accept image
page numbers only within the document. Both paths reject page numbers below 1.

Fix: [ebac361a](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/co

# pdfcpu: PDF tooling for Go and the command line [![Test](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/workflows/Test/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/actions) [![Coverage Status](https://coveralls.io/repos/github/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://coveralls.io/github/pdfcpu/pdfcpu?branch=master) [![Go Reference](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu.svg)](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0) [![Sponsor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sponsor-GitHub-%23fe8e86?logo=githubsponsors)](https://github.com/sponsors/hhrutter)

pdfcpu is a PDF processing library and command-line tool written in Go. It supports validation, optimization, encryption, signing, document assembly, content extraction, and other common PDF operations. pdfcpu supports PDF versions through PDF 2.0 (ISO 32000-2). PDF 2.0 validation support is basic and continuously improving.

  Horst Rutter, the maintainer of pdfcpu, is a member of the PDF Association.

--- ## Installation | Command-line interface | Go API | | --- | --- | | **[CLI Installation instructions](https://pdfcpu.io/getting_started/install_cli/?src=github-readme)** | **[API Installation instructions](https://pdfcpu.io/getting_started/install_api/?src=github-readme)** | --- ## Usage ### CLI Validate a PDF: ``` pdfcpu validate input.pdf ``` Merge two PDFs: ``` pdfcpu merge merged.pdf in1.pdf in2.pdf ``` ### Go API See API documentation for usage examples. ### Local images in create and form input Local images in `create`, `form fill`, and JSON/CSV `form multifill` are confined to an allowed directory.
API callers must set `conf.LocalImageRoot` to enable them. The CLI defaults to its working directory and `localImageRoot` in `config.yml` selects another root. See [local image access](https://pdfcpu.io/create/create/#local-image-access) for configuration examples, path restrictions, migration instructions and security limitations. --- ## Features * Validate, optimize, split, trim, and merge PDFs * Extract and manipulate images, fonts, and metadata * Encrypt and decrypt PDFs * Resize and rotate pages * Add and remove stamps and watermarks * Validate signature integrity, report signature evidence, and remove signatures * Manage attachments and portfolios ## Examples Selected examples:

[pages](https://pdfcpu.io/pages/pages) | | [permissions](https://pdfcpu.io/encrypt/perm_set) | [portfolio](https://pdfcpu.io/portfolio/portfolio) | [poster](https://pdfcpu.io/generate/poster) | | [viewerpref](https://pdfcpu.io/viewerpref/viewerpref) | | [watermark](https://pdfcpu.io/core/watermark) | [zoom](https://pdfcpu.io/core/zoom) | | --- ## Motivation pdfcpu aims to provide comprehensive PDF processing capabilities implemented in Go for both individual files and automated batch processing. It focuses on correctness, robustness and independence from external dependencies. --- ## Focus - comprehensive PDF processing functionality - minimal external dependencies - predictable and stable behavior --- ## Documentation * Project documentation: https://pdfcpu.io * Changelog: https://pdfcpu.io/changelog * [Contributing guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md) * [Security policy](SECURITY.md) ### CLI * Command help: `pdfcpu [command] --help` ### Go API * Package documentation: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu * API documentation: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/pkg/api * Examples: * https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/tree/master/pkg/api/test * https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/tree/master/pkg/samples --- ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. See the [contributing guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [complete list of contributors](https://github.com/pdfcpu/pdfcpu/graphs/contributors). ### Reporting PDF issues For triage, we use Adobe Acrobat Reader and macOS Preview as practical compatibility references.
Reports are especially helpful when a PDF opens in either application but cannot be processed by pdfcpu, as these cases may reveal opportunities to improve validation or parser compatibility.
If neither application can open the PDF, it is unlikely that pdfcpu will be able to process it reliably. Start by validating the file: ```bash pdfcpu validate -vv ``` Include the command, its verbose output, and a sample PDF with the report.
Please submit only files that you have permission to share and that contain no confidential information or personal data. --- ## Security Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.
See the [security policy](SECURITY.md) for private reporting instructions. --- ## Code of Conduct This project is released with a Contributor [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). By participating, you agree to abide by its terms. --- ## Disclaimer Use of pdfcpu assumes compliance with all applicable copyrights for any processed PDF content, including embedded resources such as fonts and images.
